answer: A summit cooperative hires agents to supply a meadow garden. Each supplier gains reputation only after a buyer locks payment, receives goods, and signs a delivery receipt; credit from any one buyer is capped by the actual escrow paid. Ten supplier aliases cannot multiply credit from the same shipment because its order ID is consumed at settlement. To grow influence, an attacker must finance additional fulfilled orders or bribe separate buyers. Colluding buyers can stage purchases, so randomly selected shipments face inventory audits and both parties post slashable bonds.
